items.title: Chico Freeman interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001
items.q: INTERVIEWER: And King Oliver and all those? [INTERVIEWEE] Yes. He lived with, when he first came up he stayed with my grandparents.

ctx.x: No. Well you see my history goes even further back than that. My father, my family, the Freeman family, my father has two brothers. Bruz Freeman and George Freeman. Bruz is a drummer and George is a guitarist. They all played with Charlie Parker. But prior to that, at that time they were the premier band in Chicago. My father is a legend and so are my uncles. But my grandfather is also one, he was one of the first black policemen on the Chicago police force, and my grandmother, my father’s mother and father,…
And King Oliver and all those?

Yes. He lived with, when he first came up he stayed with my grandparents. And so my grandfather was also a piano player. And so my dad grew up listening to Louis Armstrong play duets with my grandfather, and my dad and his two brothers of course. My father was actually the first one to become a musician, even though my uncle Bruz was older. He’s the oldest of the three. But he also has another history because he was a Tuskegee Airman. And he also served with Percy Heath. Percy Heath is a Tuskegee Airman. So a lot…
